body:
Thank you, I searched for issues but not pull request, my bad.

FYI, there are more issues with with the config file, see
- http://www.cmake.org/Wiki/CMake/Tutorials/Packaging

Usually one is meant to use find_package like this

``` cmake
find_package(foo REQUIRED)
...
add_executable(bar ..)
set_target_properties(bar PROPERTIES
  INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES ${foo_INCLUDE_DIRS}
)
target_link_libraries(bar
    ${foo_LIBRARIES)
)
```

You guys don't set any of these variables.  This is just inconvenient though, since a dev is required to find and open the glfw3Config.cmake and read the comments at its top, rather than having the above just work.
@MaikBeckmann Please bring those issues up in #460.

@MaikBeckmann acknowledged, will patch to export plural forms of var names
and match cmake conventions.

In making this change, would it be appropriate to mark the singular forms
(i.e. GLFW_INCLUDE_DIR) as advanced?  This caught my eye in the following
example:
http://www.cmake.org/Wiki/CMake:How_To_Find_Libraries#Writing_find_modules

On Thu, Apr 9, 2015 at 7:32 AM Camilla Berglund notifications@github.com
wrote:

> @MaikBeckmann https://github.com/MaikBeckmann Please bring those issues
> up in #460 https://github.com/glfw/glfw/pull/460.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/glfw/glfw/issues/483#issuecomment-91202452.

@ngvitovitch This is what people usually do, because it works for both simple and more involved config files,  Imagine you're writing a library  which depends on glfw.  Your config file calls find_package on glfw and aside from your own ?_INCLUDE_DIR adds GLFW_INCLUDE_DIRS to your ?_INCLUDE_DIRS.

The singular ?_INCLUDE_DIR variable is for directly reaching inside the include directory, for whatever reason (3rd party tool that requires full paths, i.e.)

issue.title: Building With CMake and installed GLFW binaries
issue.body:
[This page](http://www.glfw.org/docs/latest/build_guide.html#build_link_cmake_package) says that you can add the line
```cmake
find_package(glfw3 3.2 REQUIRED)
```
to your `CMakeLists.txt`, and be able to build the project using CMake.

It does nothing to explain where to put the glfw3 binaries, and does not provide a `Findglfw3.cmake`, `glfw3Config.cmake`, or a `glfw3-config.cmake` file, which CMake needs to evaluate the `find_package` macro. The precompiled binaries from [here](http://www.glfw.org/download.html) do not provide them either.

Simply adding the above `find_package` line to a simple `CMakeLists.txt`
```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.6)
project(Test)
add_executable(test main.cc)

find_package(glfw3 3.2 REQUIRED)
```

yields this error:
```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:6 (find_package):
  By not providing "Findglfw3.cmake" in CMAKE_MODULE_PATH this project has
  asked CMake to find a package configuration file provided by "glfw3", but
  CMake did not find one.

  Could not find a package configuration file provided by "glfw3" (requested
  version 3.2) with any of the following names:

    glfw3Config.cmake
    glfw3-config.cmake

  Add the installation prefix of "glfw3" to CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH or set
  "glfw3_DIR" to a directory containing one of the above files.  If "glfw3"
  provides a separate development package or SDK, be sure it has been
  installed.
```

Is there an example `Findglfw3.cmake`, `glfw3Config.cmake`, or `glfw3-config.cmake` file somewhere?
